title: LaMo: Self-Supervised Latent Motion Priors for Physical Realism in Video Generation
claim: Existing approaches depend on appearance-only objectives, external simulators, or teacher models; ours derives motion supervision from raw data itself.
layout: 4 columns, top-to-bottom flow, last column highlighted with ✗/✓ verdict boxes
description: Four parallel columns share the same top-to-bottom template. Each starts with a film strip of raw video showing a bouncing blue ball. An arrow leads to a blue Diffusion Model block built from bars. Below it sits a column-specific supervision source: a red diffusion-loss box (Col. 1), a physics engine/simulator panel with a wireframe mesh (Col. 2), orange teacher-model and green curated-data boxes (Col. 3), or two purple boxes for Macro Motion Drift Loss and Micro Motion Prior Guidance (Col. 4). Each column ends with a generated-video film strip and a gray verdict box. Cols. 1–3 carry red ✗ marks with drawbacks, and Col. 4 carries a green ✓ for self-supervised and plug-and-play. Col. 4 has a peach background, a star and an underlined bold title, which draw the eye first.
caption: Existing approaches to physical realism rely on hand-crafted physics simulators (Col. 2) or on foundation-model teachers and curated physics-annotated corpora (Col. 3), while the vanilla diffusion objective is dominated by per-frame appearance (Col. 1). LaMo (Col. 4) instead extracts motion supervision from the same raw video data through a Motion Drift Loss during training and Motion Prior Guidance during inference.
abstract: Modern video generators produce visually compelling clips but still struggle with physical and motion consistency, limiting their use as reliable world simulators. Existing remedies often rely on external simulators, teacher models, or curated physics-focused data. We explore a complementary self-supervised direction: extracting motion cues from the unlabeled videos already used to train video diffusion models. We propose LaMo, which formulates a latent motion prior over frame-to-frame latent changes conditioned on the current latent and prompt. This prior is exposed through two lightweight readouts: a macro motion drift used during training as a Motion Drift Loss, and a learned micro motion field used during sampling as Motion Prior Guidance. Both components are plug-and-play with existing video diffusion backbones, requiring no architectural or I/O changes. On VideoPhy, VideoPhy2, and PisaBench, LaMo improves CogVideoX backbones and outperforms recent physics-aware baselines that use external supervision. On VBench, it preserves overall generation quality while improving motion-related dimensions. These results suggest that unlabeled video contains useful motion supervision for improving physical fidelity in modern video diffusion models.
